Subject: Draft market report + preliminary geo allowance matrix

Hi Karthik / Mina,

Thanks again for the quick kickoff call yesterday. Attached is our draft market report for Q4 2026 and a first-pass geo allowance matrix built from the benchmark cohort you shared (tech IC and mid-senior product). Key highlights in the report:

- US coastal markets continue to show ~12-18% uplift vs. national median for senior IC roles.
- Mid-size EU hubs (Barcelona, Lisbon) are ~5-9% below equivalents in core Western EU markets.
- APAC dispersion remains wide; we included a recommended local index rather than a flat multiplier.

Attachments: SalaryBench_market_report_Q4_2026.pdf (full methodology) and redwood_geo_index-proposal.csv (matrix).

Questions for you both:
1) Are we comfortable anchoring to our current level definitions (L3-L6) or do you want us to normalize to the new leveling grid you mentioned?
2) Do you need separate allowances for People/Customer- facing roles vs. pure engineering? We currently present both options.

I'll be available early next week to walk through the deck and tweak the cohort if you want an alternate baseline.

Best,
Simone Park
Senior Analyst, SalaryBench

Simone — thanks for sending this over and for the solid work. Quick thoughts after a skim:

- Please normalize to the new leveling grid (we recently updated L2-L7). That will make downstream offer templates simpler.
- For now include separate columns for Customer-facing vs. IC engineering roles; we'll likely only use the customer-facing differential for sales/CS.
- Could you also produce a simplified table with recommended offer bands (min/median/max) per level + geo multiplier? The leadership team prefers a compact table for fast decisions.

Mina — bringing you into the thread so we can align on allowance thresholds and whether to bake these into official offer authorization limits.

If you can all take a look, can we target a working session Tuesday (1/12) at 11am PT to review the revised matrix? Simone, does that work for you?

Karthik / Simone — thanks for the draft. I pulled the attached internal redwood_geo_index-draft.xlsx together with our working rules. High level:

- We WILL normalize to the new leveling grid (L2-L7) as Karthik requested. I added columns mapping old levels to new.
- Proposed geo allowances (multipliers relative to national median):
  - San Francisco / NYC / London: +15% (senior ICs L5+), +12% (mid ICs L3-L4)
  - Tier-1 US markets (Seattle, Boston, Austin): +8%
  - Tier-2 US markets (Denver, Atlanta, Raleigh): +4%
  - Western EU core (Amsterdam, Dublin, Paris): +10%
  - Western EU secondary (Berlin, Madrid): +5%
  - Eastern EU & select APAC hubs: 0% to -5% depending on role

Notes / asks:
- For roles with significant customer interaction (Sales/CS/PE), I recommend adding +3% on top of the market multiplier to keep offer competitiveness.
- We should limit geo-driven exceptions in the offer queue to Senior ICs and execs; for L2-L3 we'll default to national bands to keep offers consistent.

Attachments included: redwood_geo_index-draft.xlsx (matrix & mapping), a short slide with explanation.

Simone — can you re-run the compact offer bands export using the new level map and the multipliers above (assume +/- rounding to nearest $500)? If you can circulate that before Tues 11am PT, we'll be in good shape for the working session.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Total Rewards, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Thanks team — I reviewed Mina's matrix and the approach looks appropriate. A few quick points from eng leadership perspective:

- Approve the use of the multiplier bands for L4-L6 recruiting activity effective immediately. We need this in the offer templates to reduce negotiation cycles.
- For L2-L3, agree with Mina: keep offers to national bands unless there is a documented business case. HR should add a short checkbox on the offer form to capture business justification for geo exceptions.
- Mina: please coordinate with Recruiting Ops to bake the approved multipliers into Greenhouse offer templates and flag any routing changes for approvals (>12% uplift).

Karthik — I trust you and Mina to run the working session and lock the language. If you need an exec-level signoff after Tuesday, ping me and I'll clear it.
